title: Narration: join-aware read choice (DP over each line) with --seed candidates (choose)
description: Research RS-20261014-narration (laptop ~/brennerbot_sessions): the median sentence-join reset is human (+7-9 st) but F has 29-31% of joins beyond +12 st vs human 7-12%, from deeper endings (T-007, audits). T-003: a join-aware pick among the existing reads cuts joins beyond +-7 st 29%->12%. Audit A D7: ftts --seed 1..7 gives different reads, deterministic per seed (N-10/INFRA.md:287 wrong). Build in tools/narration.py choose (portable to the skill's narrate.py): candidates = quote wrappers + --seed 1..N that pass the existing gates; DP over the line with node cost (existing score + stalls over 0.45 s, extra onset syllable, terminal events, statement-final rise) and join cost (reset beyond +12 st, register step) from a consensus of 2 trackers. Tests on synthetic candidates (no ftts): DP finds the optimum; a planted bad join is avoided; no picks => byte-identical to today's choice.

comments.author: MaroonMarsh
comments.text: P-2 pilot evidence for this bead (no repo edits; scratch scripts on the build host in ~/jmev_orch/narr_exp/P-2/ and P-2/ch07/, copies + numbers in the Brenner workspace evidence/P-2.md): DP over each line (Viterbi; node = score + gates + creak<80 Hz + rising-statement; join = reset beyond +12 st), candidates = the planner's reads plus one straight-quoted input per sentence (finisher makes 5 reads/sentence), assembled by the unchanged production choose with NARRATION_PICKS naming every sentence. F ch 02: joins beyond +12 st 3->0 of 12, creaky endings 17->11 of 21, hesitations 3->0, 16 of 21 sentences changed; F ch 07: beyond +12 11->3 of 22 (median +12.1->+8.2), creaky 21->17 of 29, cut-short reads 8->1, 21 of 29 changed. choose with the current picks reproduces production out/*.wav sample for sample (ch 02 9/9, ch 07 7/7). Needed for the tool: (1) measure each read AFTER nar.edit (the assembled sentence), not the raw span; (2) a line-level gate loop after choose: asr_batch on the lines, qa_lines + narration.py edges + validate, then exclude the failing sentence's chosen tag (cost +5) and rerun the DP: ch 02 lost the first word 'But' in the line transcript with a read whose take-level ASR had it, ch 07 lost the last word 'nine' of 07_5.1; (3) a statement ending on a rise of more than 8 st must be a gate, not a weight (07_5.4 got +16.3 st otherwise because the other reads were cut short); (4) asr_batch --known writes only new transcripts: merge before analyze/choose; (5) a reads.tsv extra input yields 4 new reads (finisher wraps it and wraps the curly read again). Not heard by anyone yet: the owner A/B page (GoldenMountain) is for that; held-out pitch trackers agree on the tail but disagree by 5-20 st on creaky joins.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
mx-4kc2 landed at 5933b2f (tools/narration.py, tools/test_narration_joint.py, tools/test_driver.py, x), pushed to main. Opt-in: nothing changes unless a run sets JOINT=1 (choose) or SEEDS=N (plan + synth).

WHAT IT DOES
- `choose --joint`: Viterbi over each line (MaroonMarsh's P-2, same weights). Node cost = 2*(1-score) + 5 per gate (cut_short, final s/z, asr_ratio<0.85) + names/hesitations/stalls + [ours] hole (unlicensed pause >0.45 s) 1.0, heard word before the first scripted one 1.0 (leading "and" ignored), statement rise 0.25/st, creaky ending 1.0 (P-2's definition), terminal pitch event 2.0; join cost = reset past +12 st (1.0 + 0.2/st) + [ours] register step past 4 st at 0.1/st. A director's pick is forced; ties go to narrate.py's read (+0.02 on any other). Reads moved off narrate.py's pick carry `joint` {from, node, join} in report.json; with --joint off, analyze() keeps the report's key order, so a run is byte for byte the old one (tested).
- `plan --seeds N`: every planned read again with `ftts --seed 1..N`, tags content-addressed (`<id>__s<j>__<hash of base tag + seed>`), listed in work/seeds.tsv and NOT takes.tsv (tts_batch.py would synthesize them without the seed under a seeded tag). `synth WORK` makes them through tts_batch.py's own batch (resumable, serial retries) with `--seed`.
- `exclude`: after the line-level gates (qa_lines, edges) fail a joint build, the reads the joint choice moved in the failing lines go to work/joint_exclude.txt (priced as a failed gate); `./x <slug> narrate` loops choose -> line ASR -> gates -> exclude, at most 12 rounds, stops when nothing new is excluded. A line with every moved read excluded is narrate.py's pick.
- x: `JOINT=1 SEEDS=2 ./x <slug> narrate`; uv gets praat-parselmouth only when JOINT is set.

DEVIATION FROM THE BEAD TEXT (with the evidence): "consensus of 2 trackers" is Praat for the costs + a Viterbi autocorrelation path as a held-out second tracker (counted beside Praat's in the run's `joint:` line; a terminal event needs both). Reason, measured on chapter 02 (12 joins of narrate.py's picks): On 10 of the 12 joins Praat reads the previous sentence's ending at 62-75 Hz (the others 91 and 114); narrate.py's autocorrelation tracker (folded) reads those sentences' endings at 87-163 Hz and the Viterbi path at 92-255 Hz. Against Praat, mean(Praat - folded autocorr) = +8.8 st, within 3 st on 2 of 12 joins; mean(Praat - Viterbi) = +6.1 st, within 3 st on 1 of 12. Joins past +12 st: Praat 5, folded autocorr 0, Viterbi 2. My first version (min of the two numpy trackers) therefore moved 2 of 21 sentences and saw "0 bad joins before"; the research's gate (T-007, skill G9) is Praat's. --joint needs `uv run --with praat-parselmouth` and says so if it is missing.

REAL DATA (build host; chapter 02 of Video F, P-2's 21 sentences x 5 reads, copies in a scratch dir, P-2's own directory untouched)
- narrate.py's pick vs --joint, Praat on each sentence as assembled (edit() output): joins past +12 st 5 -> 0 of 12; median reset +11.7 -> +8.1 st; max +23.2 -> +11.9; creaky endings 17 -> 11 of 21 (MaroonMarsh's P-2 numbers: 17 -> 11); held-out second tracker: 2 -> 0 of 12; 14 of 21 sentences differ from narrate.py's pick; 19 of 21 picks equal MaroonMarsh's P-2 round-2 picks (narrate.py's own picks equal them on 7 of 21).
- Line-level loop on the real takes: round 0: qa_lines 0.995 PASS, validate PASS, edges FAIL "02_4.0: first word 'but' is not in the line's transcript" (the lost "But" of P-2; the read is the doubled-quote wrap, tag 02_4__s0__a5f6adb7, the same tag MaroonMarsh excluded). `exclude` priced that one read; round 1: qa_lines mean 1.000, validate PASS, edges PASS. One exclusion round, as in P-2's two.
- Real ftts, seeds: "Take thirty-five times five." (michael, 0.1.11) = 1.81 s unseeded, 2.12 s seed 1, 2.35 s seed 2; the quoted wraps likewise (3.51 / 2.48 / 2.05 s; 2.67 / 2.96 / 1.86 s). A fresh `synth` into a second work dir from the same seeds.tsv gave byte-identical files for all 6 seeded reads (md5 equal). Calls went through the lock wrapper.

TESTS (all green on the build host in a clean tree built from the committed content, mode of narration.py aside)
- tools/test_narration_joint.py, 32 tests, run with `uv run --no-project --with numpy --with praat-parselmouth`: Viterbi = brute force over 40 random layered problems; a planted 13.6 st join is avoided (the way out costs 0.02 in score); with every extra cost zero it equals narrate.py's stable-sort pick (50 random score sets with ties); each node cost (gates, hole, rise, question exempt, creak, terminal needs both trackers, extra onset); join cost = Praat's reset, second tracker held out, price starts past +12 st, register step; both trackers on synthetic buzz (glide, strong second harmonic, a 15 st terminal jump, silence); seed tags; `plan --seeds` leaves takes.tsv and the unseeded plan.json byte-identical and a later plan without --seeds restores them; `synth` against a stand-in ftts (right --seed per read, second synth calls nothing); `choose --joint` end to end on a two-sentence line (moves the second sentence off a +15.7 st join to a +9.0 st one, reports `joint.from`, first sentence's samples unchanged; a director's pick kept; where no join is bad the line WAV and report.json are byte-identical to the run without --joint); the exclusion loop converges to narrate.py's pick and never excludes it.
- tools/test_driver.py, +4 tests: the narrate command with every tool a recorder: without JOINT/SEEDS the call sequence is plan, synth, choose, edges and no --seeds/--joint/praat; with both, plan has --seeds=2, choose runs twice with --joint after one exclude; stops when exclude finds nothing new; gives up after 12 rounds.
- Also green on the same tree: test_narration_picks 4, onset 6, edges 5, sibilant 7, test_driver 30 in all. ubs: 0 critical on the four files. No Rust touched: no cargo, clippy or bcheck run, and none claimed.

NOT DONE / OPEN
- Nobody has listened. Whether the joint reads sound better, and whether creak is a defect (the creak weight 1.0 is P-2's), are the owner's A/B.
- Weights are P-2's one-shot, untuned; register 0.1/st, terminal 2.0, hole 1.0 and onset 1.0 are mine and unvalidated against his ear. The extra-onset cue is ASR-based (a heard word before the first scripted one), tested on text, not yet on a real 14_3.0-type take; terminal events fire on synthetic buzz but chapter 02 holds none to move.
- Only chapter 02 measured on real takes (MaroonMarsh has chapter 07 running). Seeds are not yet used on a real video: a SEEDS=N run synthesizes (1+N) x reads and needs the lock.
- `synth` carries a copy of tts_batch.synth's body (it must add --seed); an upstream `--seed` in tts_batch.py would remove the copy (skills repo, not this bead).
- exclude only prices reads the joint choice moved; a failing line whose failing read is narrate.py's own stays red, as it did.
- AGENTS.md doctrine 5 already says seeds are live (1b5ed02); the narration skill's SCORING-AND-SELECTION still says narrate.py choose picks per sentence, until the joint choice is ported there ("portable to the skill's narrate.py": tools/narration.py is a wrapper around it, the DP functions are pure and move as they are).

one about the very best "visual proofs" in math", with his thread of four favourites (Nicomachus's
sum of cubes as slabs tiling a square; 1/4 + 1/16 + ... = 1/3 in a quartered square; (a + b)^2,

owner's four plus the best classics, each animated as a real proof (pieces move into place, then

picture can lie (Curry's missing square) and what turns a picture into a proof. This lane runs
P0-P5 (brief, facts + oracle, storyboard + R1, script, build, drafts read as contact and cue
sheets) and stops for the owner; narration, score and 4K follow his review. Voice michael;
12-16 min; chapters <= 85 s. Crate: explainer_corpus/visual_proofs.

title: Video E (fair_coin): unify 3D-bulged Flip across 03_3, 05_2, and 08_4, wire chapter moods and Theme::Open/Theme::Resolved in score.rs, and rebuild stems + scored draft
description:
## Background & Motivation
In Video E (`explainer_corpus/fair_coin`), commit `90693cf` guarded the midpoint (`|e - 0.5| < 0.01`) of the custom `Flip` animation in `src/chapters/every_coin.rs:190-220` (`03_3`), which reflects the `HT` region across the `x = y` diagonal with a 3D-like normal bulge `(-1, 1)/sqrt(2) * 0.25 * sin(pi * e)` so the polygon does not collapse to a collinear segment at `e = 0.5`.

However, two later chapters perform the exact same conceptual symmetry reflection across the diagonal using raw `fmn::Transform::new` (linear 2D point interpolation):
1. `src/chapters/where_it_breaks.rs:658` (beat `05_2`, reflecting the `HT` box into the `TH` box across the diagonal to show their areas are unequal when `p != 0.5`).
2. `src/chapters/loaded_dice.rs:623, 646` (beat `08_4`, reflecting the `1-then-2` and `1-then-3` cells across the main diagonal of the 6×6 die table).
Under linear 2D `Transform::new`, every vertex `(x_i, y_i)` moves linearly to `(y_i, x_i)`, so at `e = 0.5` every vertex satisfies `x_i(0.5) = y_i(0.5) = (x_i + y_i)/2`: the entire rectangle collapses onto the 1D line `y = x` (zero area) mid-animation!

Additionally, in `explainer_corpus/fair_coin/src/score.rs:28-29`, `moods: &[]` and `themes: &[]` are currently empty slices, whereas sibling videos (`mental_math`, `bayesian_search`, `eigen_engineering`) populate per-chapter `Mood` transitions and `Theme::Open` / `Theme::Resolved` listen-window cues so `explainer_score` voices the opening motif and closing resolution at the video's structural bookends.

## Implementation Steps
1. **Unify `Flip` in `src/chapters/draw.rs`:**
   - Promote `Flip` from `every_coin.rs:190-220` into `draw.rs` (accepting `from: MobjectId`, `to: MobjectId`, `duration: f64`, and an optional bulge amplitude or default `0.25` along `(-1.0, 1.0) / sqrt(2)` with midpoint guard `if (e - 0.5).abs() < 0.01 { e += 0.01; }`).
   - Replace `Transform::new(ht_ghost, th_target, 1.4)` in `where_it_breaks.rs:658` (`05_2`) and `Transform::new(from_a, to_a, 1.2)` / `Transform::new(from_b, to_b, 1.2)` in `loaded_dice.rs:623, 646` (`08_4`) with `draw::Flip::new(...)`.
2. **Wire `moods` and `themes` in `src/score.rs`:**
   - Populate `themes: &[("01_5", Theme::Open), ("10_4", Theme::Resolved)]` (matching the listen windows in `01_the_gamblers_problem` and `10_how_good_is_it` / `11_your_pocket_has_no_coin`).
   - Populate chapter `moods` across chapters `01..11` matching the narrative progression (e.g. `Mood::Wonder` -> `Mood::Bright` -> `Mood::Tension` on `05_where_it_breaks` -> `Mood::Calm` / `Mood::Bright` on resolution).
3. **Rebuild Stems & Scored Draft on the Build Host:**
   - Because `score::identity()` changes `score::fingerprint(identity, timeline)`, re-render chapters `03`, `05`, `08` at 540p (`./x fair_coin draft 03`, `05`, `08`), then run `./x fair_coin score` (verifying all 11 chapters pass Score QA with narrator F0 `75.5-163.3 Hz` clear) and `./x fair_coin scored`.

## Verification & Testing Requirements
- Unit test in `draw.rs` proving that `Flip` keeps polygon shoelace area strictly bounded away from zero across 100 sampled values `e in [0.0, 1.0]`.
- Unit test in `score.rs` verifying `identity.themes` contains `Theme::Open` and `Theme::Resolved`, `identity.moods` is non-empty, and zero minor-ninth clashes occur against the progression chords.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `./x fair_coin facts-check`, and `ubs` clean.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Move/expose 3D-bulged Flip (with midpoint guard |e - 0.5| < 0.01 and normal bulge) in explainer_corpus/fair_coin/src/chapters/draw.rs and use it in every_coin.rs (03_3), where_it_breaks.rs:658 (05_2), and loaded_dice.rs:623,646 (08_4). 2. Populate moods and themes (01_5 Theme::Open, 10_4 Theme::Resolved) in fair_coin/src/score.rs. 3. Add unit tests for non-zero Flip polygon area across e in [0, 1] and score themes/moods. 4. Re-render affected chapters (03, 05, 08), re-run ./x fair_coin score (11/11 QA pass) and ./x fair_coin scored, and verify contact sheets.

Refinement Round 1 (Exact Code Anchors & Mathematical Details):
1. every_coin.rs:190-220 defines struct Flip { from: MobjectId, to: MobjectId, duration: f64 } which interpolates corresponding points across the diagonal x = y with normal offset (-1.0, 1.0) / sqrt(2) * 0.25 * (pi * e).sin() and midpoint guard if (e - 0.5).abs() < 0.01 { e += 0.01; }.
2. Move struct Flip into src/chapters/draw.rs (pub struct Flip) and replace:
   - src/chapters/where_it_breaks.rs:658 (beat 05_2): stage.play(Transform::new(ht_ghost, th_target, 1.4)) -> stage.play(draw::Flip::new(ht_ghost, th_target, 1.4))
   - src/chapters/loaded_dice.rs:623, 646 (beat 08_4): Transform::new(from_a, to_a, 1.2) and Transform::new(from_b, to_b, 1.2) -> draw::Flip::new(...)
3. In src/score.rs:28-29, replace moods: &[] and themes: &[] with:

4. Note on stem invalidation: changing score::identity() changes score::fingerprint(identity, timeline), which Kit::finish checks when mixing scored chapters. Therefore ./x fair_coin score MUST be re-run before ./x fair_coin scored.

1. **Pre-Flight Gate Check:**
   - Ensure working tree for `explainer_corpus/fair_coin` and `crates/` is clean and committed (`G8` refuses `--fmn-local` or dirty trees).

   - Render all 11 chapters (`01_the_gamblers_problem` through `11_your_pocket_has_no_coin`) at `3840x2160 @ 60 fps`, BT.709, using the single runner-wrapped encoder across all chapters so stream-copy concatenation succeeds without codec parameter mismatch.

comments.text: CORRECTION to my earlier comment and to commits 31bbfe3/01014b9: 'set_points refuses a run of another size' is wrong (SunnyMarsh's probe was right). Probed on a bare stage with set_points's Result printed: it is Ok for 2->49 vertices, points do change. The real cause: a mobject whose point count changes WHILE A FADE-IN IS PLAYING over it ends the fade at the opacity it began at (stroke opacity 0.016 for the curve, 0.058 for a ray) and stays invisible; same size is fine (1.0), and a resize after the fade has ended is fine (1.0). The curve (14_6) and rays (11_1) were built as 2 vertices and resized in the first frame of their fade-in. My earlier state probes did not fade in, so they passed on the old code too; they now run the chapter's order (updater on the scene, fade_in_all) and assert opacity > 0.99; checked red on the two-vertex build, green on the full-size build (one_idea.rs, where_modes_rule.rs, pushed). Any mobject an updater resizes after a fade-in starts is exposed to this: grep for polylines built with fewer vertices than their updater writes.

title: Video F (mental_math): drive 04_4 waver continuously through END_HOLD_S, wire 14_3 three-turn three-pluck recall beat, and verify scored draft
description:
## Background & Motivation
In Video F (`explainer_corpus/mental_math`), commit `05a1ba5` fixed the `u64` addition overflow in `model::near_fifty` (`model.rs:302-316`), deduplicated `waver` into `src/chapters/draw.rs`, and added `score.rs` unit tests. Two high-leverage visual/audio polish items remain from the code and storyboard audit:

1. **Frozen `waver` during `04_4`'s `END_HOLD_S` (`src/chapters/by_parts.rs:344`):**
   - In chapter `04_by_parts` (`04_4`), the juggling items' vertical oscillation is driven by an `add_dt_updater` reading a `ValueTracker` (`waver`) that is only advanced when `waver.animate_value(...)` is explicitly played.
   - At line 344, the chapter ends with `kit.music_breath(stage, END_HOLD_S)` (`1.5 s`), which calls `stage.wait_frames(...)` without advancing `waver`. As a result, the juggling balls freeze motionless in mid-air for the final 1.5 seconds of the chapter.
   - Driving `waver` across `END_HOLD_S` (or stepping `waver.animate_value(END_HOLD_S, ...)` inside the breath window while recording the music breath mark) keeps the motion alive right up to the chapter cut.
2. **Closing recall beat `14_3` three-pluck sonification (`src/chapters/near_something_you_know.rs:482`):**
   - In chapter `14` (`14_3`, `near_something_you_know.rs:482`), the closing callback highlights the three core mental-math patterns in sequence (`turns` loop). Wiring this beat with its three-pluck sonification from `src/chapters/sound.rs` (and verifying the `score` timeline marks) gives the visual callback its intended musical punctuation.

## Implementation Steps
1. Update `explainer_corpus/mental_math/src/chapters/by_parts.rs` around line 344 so `waver` advances continuously through `END_HOLD_S` while preserving the chapter's exact frame count and music breath mark.
2. Update `explainer_corpus/mental_math/src/chapters/near_something_you_know.rs` around line 482 (`14_3`) and `src/chapters/sound.rs` so the three-turn visual highlight triggers the three-pluck sonification cleanly.
3. Add unit tests in `by_parts.rs` (verifying non-zero y-displacement of the juggling items across `END_HOLD_S`) and `sound.rs` / `near_something_you_know.rs`.
4. Re-render chapters `04` and `14` on the build host, run `./x mental_math score` (verifying 14/14 chapters pass Score QA) and `./x mental_math scored`, and inspect the updated frames.
acceptance_criteria: 1. In explainer_corpus/mental_math/src/chapters/by_parts.rs:344 (04_4), drive the waver tracker continuously through END_HOLD_S (1.5 s) instead of freezing during music_breath. 2. In near_something_you_know.rs:482 (14_3), pair the three turns of the closing recall beat with the three-pluck sonification from sound.rs. 3. Add unit tests verifying continuous waver motion during 04_4's hold and sound mark/sonification alignment in 14_3. 4. Re-render chapters 04 and 14, re-run ./x mental_math score and ./x mental_math scored, and verify contact sheets.

Advance waver across END_HOLD_S (e.g. record the music_breath mark on kit and play waver.animate_value(waver.get() + END_HOLD_S, END_HOLD_S) with Linear rate) so the juggling motion never freezes at the end of chapter 04.

description:

Once Video F (`mental_math`) completes its narration & initial score (`mx-e-a-f-ms4.8`), `04_4` continuous `waver` + `14_3` three-pluck polish (`mx-e-a-f-ms4.10`), and owner review of `renders/mental_math_scored_watch.mp4`, this bead executes the Gate G8 4K60 final render, PCM master assembly, and strict verification.

1. **Pre-Flight Gate Check:**

   - Assemble the 4K60 master (`explainer_corpus/mental_math/renders/final/mental_math_master.mp4`) with PCM master audio and rebuild SRT/WebVTT captions.
4. **Strict G8 Verification (`./x mental_math verify`):**
   - Run `verify_video.sh` (`3840x2160`, `60 fps`, `BT.709`, `-16 LUFS ± 1.0`, `<= -1.0 dBTP`, `A/V <= 0.2 s`, null test, full decode).

gone missing, men are trapped, & time is running out. How can we possibly find them in time?"
The method is the hero: a prior map of cells built from weighted scenarios, detection probability
(the chance of finding = the chance it is there times the chance you would see it), Bayes' rule after
a failed search, planning by where the next effort buys the most (Koopman's random search formula),
and drift under time pressure. Stories, each checked against primary sources: Palomares 1966,
Scorpion 1968 (all 99 men were lost; never implied otherwise), Air France 447 (2011), Coast Guard
rescues. Quizzes with a visible countdown. This lane runs P0-P5 (brief, facts + oracle, storyboard +
R1, script, build, drafts read as contact and cue sheets) and stops for the owner; narration, score
and 4K follow his review. Voice michael; 11-15 min; chapters <= 85 s. Crate:
explainer_corpus/bayesian_search.

## Background & Motivation
In Video J (`explainer_corpus/matrix_exponential`), recent commits have resolved nearly all code, documentation, and dense-read issues:
- Commit `224e0ba` authored `docs/description.md` covering all 16 chapters, exact statements, programmer notes (`IBM 370` vs IEEE `f32`), and Standard Model gauge group (`Z6`), passing all 25 rows of `docs/protected.tsv` (`protected_check.py` 25/25 pass), and expanded `glyphs::DIGITS`.
- Commits `3b3954e` and `3b5d667` (`PeachPuma`) fixed `EmeraldOwl`'s dense-read findings across chapters `01–16`:
  - `12_5` (`heat_and_chance.rs`): `put_the_i_in()` rewinds the panel's clock back to `0` (`0.8 s`) as the exponent changes to `-itL`.
  - `13_5` (`how_computers_do_it.rs`): `eigen_pointer()` and `who_and_when()` spaced cleanly (`> 0.3` unit clearance above the lower-third).
  - `14_5` (`order_matters.rs`): `"AB - BA ="` laid out by measure with `NAME_GAP = 0.35` left of the grid's left bracket.
  - `15_2` (`the_doorway.rs`) & `03_3`, `06_3`, `08_3`: quiz cards ask the exact question the voice asks (`script.tsv` asserted).

title: Epic Video G: Why Robot Arms Think in Lie Groups (lie_robotics)
description:
Produce Video G, working title "Why Robot Arms Think in Lie Groups", from the owner's request: "let's
make another video about the connection between Lie groups and robotics. Use the content from my
/dp/cmaes_explainer project, including the model of the Kuka robot arm and others you can find
online." and "Throughout the video, combine clear explanations, worked examples, and quizzes with
pauses before the answers." Robots: the KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820 (every number from the xacro the
owner's project vendors, cited by path, never copied), the KMR iiwa mecanum base (planar motion,
SE(2)) and the Unitree G1 (a floating base in SE(3)). Arc: orientations do not add; rotations as a
group; why three angles fail; velocities and the exponential map; SE(2); SE(3) and screws; the arm as
a product of exponentials; the Jacobian, singularities and the seventh joint; inverse kinematics as

- score.rs: the title card's window 01_3 plays the motif open (theme), two tests.

title: Video B: fact sheet + oracle.py (P1)
description:
Fact sheet rows B-F1..B-F28 (plan §10.5); oracle.py reusing docs/research/raptorq_gf256/scripts (gf256np, rank_probs, toy_examples, misc_facts; measured counts pinned as recorded constants with their output file). Resolve the (to verify) items before narration: Erdos 1948 irrationality citation; RAID-6 Q = sum 2^i D_i in 0x11D and the 51-weight limit under 0x11B; QR codes' polynomial (285) against ISO/IEC 18004; whether RaptorQ (vs Raptor) is in 3GPP TS 26.346 (script says 'older sibling' until confirmed); Intel GFNI's polynomial (only if used).

Gate G1 (after the crate exists): `./x raptorq_gf256 facts-check` PASS (binary `facts` == oracle.py key by key; integers exact, others to 1e-9). Before the crate exists: oracle.py runs standalone with `python3 -I` and prints every value in the fact sheet.
Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.
close_reason: Done at 9ebdf36: docs/facts/raptorq_gf256/{oracle.py,fact-sheet.md}. python3 -I oracle.py prints 297 keys in about 4 s, identical across runs; 22 internal cross-checks. All ledger rows B-F1..B-F28 match (spot-checked independently: 3*7=9, 2*128=29, 128*4=58, 150*3=167, 2*142=1, 0x57*0x83=0x31 under 0x11D, 0xC1 under 0x11B, ord 2 = 51 under 0x11B). Measured RaptorQ counts (B-F21 ablations, B-F22 Monte Carlo) are recorded constants, checked against their files in docs/research/raptorq_gf256/scripts/results/ on every run; B-F23 is quoted from RFC 6330 section 5.8. Open items: Erdos 1948 verified (the paper's theorem); RAID-6 verified (Anvin: 0x11D, g = {02}, '{02} is not a generator of the AES representation'); QR's 285 verified against ISO/IEC 18004:2006 clause 6.5.2 (2024 edition not checked); 3GPP TS 26.346 specifies Raptor (RFC 5053), not RaptorQ, so 'older sibling' stays; GFNI is unused by the script. Plan text corrected: element orders, 2 not a generator under AES's polynomial, 0.39215% exact. Caveat: the single 1-in-10^6 failure at K+2 cannot confirm the standard's requirement (95% CI 2.5e-8 to 5.6e-6); B-F18 / B-F25 Monte Carlo depend on CPython's RNG and must be pinned for G1.

title: explainer_kit: exact 8-bit colour via the P010 wire (ffmpeg writes the 8-bit stream)
description:
Found by spike S-5 (commit ae23be9). franken_manim's 8-bit NV12 wire is about 1.5 Cb codes short on dark blue. The corpus background #0E1116 is written as Y 30, Cb 129, Cr 126, where exact BT.709 limited-range codes are 30.37 / 130.50 / 126.48. The result is a slightly green-black background (#0D1112 on screen instead of #0E1116), visible under a contrast stretch and present in every 8-bit deliverable so far, v5's master included.

How it was measured:
- a CRF-0 (lossless) fmn render of a flat background, decoded to raw yuv420p;
- fmn's RGBA8 PNG frames are exact (14, 17, 22);
- fmn's P010 path writes 121 / 522 / 507, which is 130.5 x 4 for Cb, exact;
- ffmpeg's own RGB-to-yuv420p conversion writes 29 / 130 / 126.

The bias is introduced in fmn's fused NV12 conversion. fmn-frame's rgba_to_nv12 on the same pixels would round correctly.

Fix on the corpus side, without touching franken_manim: render on the P010 wire and let ffmpeg write the 8-bit H.264 stream. The kit's QualityRunner already rewrites the encode argv. It can replace fmn's `-pix_fmt yuv420p10le` (P010 in, 10-bit out) with `-pix_fmt yuv420p`, so swscale converts 10 to 8 bits with its rounding and dither, which also helps against banding. Set `file_writer.pixel_format = "p010le"` in delivery renders, including the CLI's options() after delivery_options.

Acceptance:
- A CRF-0 render of a flat #0E1116 frame decodes to Cb within 0.5 of 130.5 and Y within 0.5 of 30.37, against today's 129.
- The same check runs on a palette colour (Hoeffding yellow #FFD866).
- The 4K fps cost of the 2x pipe payload is measured (P010 is 25 MB per frame against NV12's 12 MB) and noted.
- The output stays 8-bit High profile H.264 with BT.709 tags; verify_video.sh passes.
- An integration test in the kit asserts the codes, with ffmpeg on PATH as the CLI tests already require.

Upstream: the same evidence goes into the franken_manim issue packet (U-18; filing needs the owner's OK).

Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.
close_reason: Done at 3851db4, by a simpler fix than this bead proposed. The cause was not fmn's NV12 conversion. fmn's encode argv declares no colour space or range on its raw input (only on the output), so ffmpeg converts the frames from its default matrix. Exact NV12 bytes (30, 130, 126) fed through fmn's argv shape reproduce Cb 129, and come through exact once the input is tagged. The kit's runner now inserts -colorspace bt709 -color_range <output's> before -i - on raw-video jobs, and the NV12 wire stays (no 2x pipe payload, no P010). Acceptance: lossless (CRF 0) renders through the delivery encoder decode to background #0E1116 = 30/130/126 (BT.709 30.36/130.50/126.48) and yellow #FFD866 = 202/74/150 (201.56/74.00/149.72), all within 0.5 code (tests/exact_colour.rs). Planted negative: fmn's own argv gives background Cb 129 and yellow 203/75/146. Unit test for the argv (inserted once; mux jobs untouched); the VideoToolbox test restated to its intent (no rate control; only the input tags added). Output stays 8-bit High H.264 with BT.709 tags. The fps cost is none: the wire is unchanged.

title: explainer_kit: deterministic in-memory scene telemetry & invariant audit helpers (I-1..I-5)
description:
## Background & Motivation
Currently, individual explainer crates (`matrix_exponential`, `eigen_engineering`, `bayesian_search`, `lie_robotics`) have written local, ad-hoc test helpers (`draw::watch_dwell`, `marks.rs`, `QuizAudit`) to step chapters in-memory using the scratch voice (`run_voiced`) and inspect mobject visibility, dwell durations, and quiz countdown timing. However, `crates/explainer_kit` lacks a unified, reusable scene telemetry and invariant verification harness that all 11 explainers in `explainer_corpus/` can call from their `#[cfg(test)]` suites.

Several subtle `franken_manim` engine traps and 3Blue1Brown visual-continuity defects recur across videos and are expensive to discover only after 540p/4K renders and human montage reads:
1. **Retained-renderer `fade_in` point-count resize trap** (discovered in `eigen_engineering` `mx-e-a-e-k-oq4.7` `f63a276`): mutating a mobject's Bézier point count (`set_points`) while a `fade_in` animation is active freezes its opacity at ~0.02–0.06 for the rest of the scene.
2. **Premature quiz answer reveals or sub-second post-reveal flashes** (`REVIEW-AND-CONTINUITY.md` §5): quiz answers appearing before the countdown ring hits zero, or cards fading out <1.0 s after reveal as the next spoken line begins.
3. **Lower-third reading-rate starvation**: `"precisely:"`, `"for programmers:"`, or `"who and when:"` bands appearing late in a spoken line and getting wiped <2.5 s later by the next beat.
4. **Black-stage seams between beats**: sequential `fade_out` followed by `fade_in` (instead of overlapped crossfade or `hand_over`) leaving the stage empty for 0.5–7.0 s under spoken narration.
5. **Collinear polygon collapse on 2D reflections**: linear point interpolation across a mirror axis collapsing polygon area to zero at midpoint `e = 0.5`.

## Mathematical & Technical Specification (Invariants I-1..I-5)
Stepping a chapter scene at 10–15 fps in-memory (`stage.scene_mut()` without pixel rasterization or FFmpeg encoding) takes <0.5 s in `cargo test` and allows every chapter to prove five deterministic invariants:

1. **Invariant I-1 — Bézier Point-Count Stability Under Opacity Transitions:**
   For every mobject `m` in the scene arena at consecutive sampled frames `t_{k-1}, t_k`:
   If `|alpha_m(t_k) - alpha_m(t_{k-1})| > 1e-4` and `0.01 < alpha_m(t_k) < 0.99` (i.e. `m` is actively fading in or out), then `points_m(t_k).len() == points_m(t_{k-1}).len()`.
2. **Invariant I-2 — Causal Quiz Masking & Post-Zero Answer Dwell:**
   For every registered quiz with countdown window `[t_ring, t_zero]`:
   - Answer mobjects satisfy `alpha_ans(t) == 0` for all `t < t_zero - 1/fps`.
   - Within `0.5 s` after `t_zero`, `alpha_ans(t) >= 0.95`.
   - The answer remains on-scene with `alpha_ans(t) >= 0.90` for `dwell >= max(1.5 s, W_ans / 3.5 wps)` (and until the first spoken sentence after the countdown completes).
3. **Invariant I-3 — Lower-Third Legibility & Reading-Rate Gate:**
   Every lower-third with word count `W` remains on-scene at `alpha >= 0.90` for `dwell >= max(2.5 s, W / 4.0 wps)` and stays within the lower-third vertical band (`y in [-3.85, -2.85]`) with zero bounding-box intersection against stage content (`y > -2.75`).
4. **Invariant I-4 — Non-Empty Stage Under Spoken Narration:**
   For every spoken line `L_i` spanning `[t_start, t_end]`, over `[t_start + 0.6 s, t_end - 0.3 s]`, the total visible non-backdrop bounding-box area satisfies `sum_{m notin Backdrop} alpha_m(t) * Area(bbox(m)) > 0.25 stage units^2`.
5. **Invariant I-5 — Non-Collinear Reflection Morph Area Gate:**
   Provide a shared geometric helper/assertion verifying that any reflected polygon morph maintains shoelace area `|A(e)| >= A_min > 0` across all `e in [0, 1]` via out-of-line normal bulge `b * sin(pi * e) * n_perp` and midpoint guard `|e - 0.5| < 0.01`.

## Files to Touch
- `crates/explainer_kit/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/explainer_kit/src/lint.rs` (or a new `crates/explainer_kit/src/telemetry.rs` module exported from `lib.rs`)

## Verification & Testing Requirements
- Unit tests in `crates/explainer_kit` exercising synthetic passing and failing scenes for each invariant (I-1 through I-5), verifying that each failure produces a structured diagnostic (`chapter`, `line_id`, `scene_time_s`, `mob_label`, `expected`, `actual`).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` in `crates/explainer_kit`, and `ubs` clean.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Shared telemetry/audit module in crates/explainer_kit steps chapter scenes in-memory without pixel rasterization or FFmpeg encoding (<0.5s per chapter). 2. Enforces Invariant I-1 (Bezier point-count stability under opacity transitions), Invariant I-2 (causal quiz masking & post-zero dwell), Invariant I-3 (lower-third legibility & reading-rate gate), Invariant I-4 (non-empty stage under spoken narration), and Invariant I-5 (non-collinear reflection morph area check). 3. Emits structured failure diagnostics (chapter, line_id, scene_time_s, mob_label, expected, actual). 4. Unit tests in explainer_kit pass cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings.
close_reason: Landed commit 787fef2: added crates/explainer_kit/src/telemetry.rs (re-exported in lib.rs) with SceneFrame, SceneRecorder, InvariantDiagnostic, guard_reflection_param, normal_bulge_offset, shoelace_area, and deterministic invariant checkers I-1..I-5. Verified on build host: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -p explainer_kit --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test -p explainer_kit --lib (76/76 pass including planted-negative unit and live headless run_scene tests), ubs Critical 0.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Refinement Round 1 (Technical Architecture & API Specification):
- In crates/explainer_kit/src/lint.rs (or telemetry.rs), provide a headless scene stepper (e.g. SceneTelemetry::record(stage, fps)) that samples stage.scene() at each frame step during scratch-voice or timeline-backed test runs.
- At each sampled frame k (time t_k = k / fps), record per-MobjectId snapshots: (opacity, points.len(), bounding_box, is_backdrop, tag/role).
- Invariant I-1 (fade_in/fade_out point-count stability): if (opacity_k - opacity_{k-1}).abs() > 1e-4 and 0.01 < opacity_k < 0.99, assert points_len_k == points_len_{k-1}. This catches the exact franken_manim retained-renderer defect encountered in eigen_engineering (f63a276) where mutating a truss polygon's vertex count mid-fade froze its alpha at ~0.04.
- Invariant I-2 (quiz reveal causality & post-zero dwell): for each QuizWindow { line_id, ring_start_s, ring_zero_s, first_sentence_after_s, answer_mobs, word_count }, assert max opacity of answer_mobs is 0.0 for all t < ring_zero_s - 1.0/fps, reaches >= 0.95 within 0.5 s after ring_zero_s, and stays >= 0.90 until max(ring_zero_s + max(1.5, word_count as f64 / 3.5), first_sentence_after_s - 0.05).
- Invariant I-3 (lower-third reading-rate & band clearance): for each LowerThirdWindow { line_id, mob_id, word_count }, assert full-opacity dwell (opacity >= 0.90) is >= max(2.5, word_count as f64 / 4.0) s, bbox.y_min >= -3.85, bbox.y_max <= -2.85, and zero bbox intersection with non-backdrop stage mobjects above y = -2.75.
- Invariant I-4 (non-empty stage under speech): for each spoken line [t_start, t_end], over [t_start + 0.6, t_end - 0.3], assert sum of alpha_m * area(bbox_m) for non-backdrop mobjects > 0.25 stage units^2.

title: explainer_kit: script.tsv parser, Narrator, exact cue/timeline recorder, cue validation
description:

- Placement gain: 0 dB under the new score engine (D-21; the template's -9.4 dB was a balance for the old pad). Keep it a parameter.
- NEW timeline recorder: logs every cue in insertion order with path + SHA-256, integer time.frames() and fps, time_offset and gain as exact f64 bits, decoded rate/channels/frames; authored marks (kit.mark), music breaths (kit.music_breath), listen windows; and the scene's total frames. Never {:.3}-second strings (one 60 fps frame prints as 0.017 s = 816 samples, not 800).
- NEW cue validation at add time: <= 64 MiB, parseable by fmn's decoder formats (u8/s16/s24/s32/f32, mono/stereo), finite samples, final chunk sizes (fmn only reports these after the whole render).
- Timeline pass: a construct-only run of a scene dumps its timeline JSON (add_sound is a no-op in skip mode, so the recorder is the kit's own).

Tests: parser rejects malformed scripts with line numbers; timeline JSON round trip; a cue at frame 1 of a 60 fps scene records 800 samples exactly; validation rejects a 65 MiB file, a NaN-containing f32 WAV and a truncated header (planted negatives).

title: explainer_score: PolyBLEP oscillators, OU drift, TPT/SVF/ZDF ladder, FIR, DC blocker

title: explainer_score: score DSL, buses and stem render (two-pass, per act, sliced per chapter)
description:
Score DSL (plan §7.4-7.5): Identity (key, mode, tempo with +-8% elastic phrasing, palette, leitmotif in scale degrees, seed) and ChapterPlan (harmony with chords of 4-16 s changing only in gaps or intra-sentence pauses >= 0.2 s and never within 150 ms of a speech onset; an intensity arc 0..1 driving density, cutoff, register spread and reverb send; cues anchored to line ids, marks and listen windows; cue types: reveal stinger, transition swell, aha resolution, tick/counter, pizzicato count, whoosh/riser, sonification). Mixer: buses (bed, colour, cue, sfx) -> sends -> duck + pocket -> stem; music stem true peak <= -12 dBTP. Two-pass (D-22): render each act (or the whole video) from the combined timeline, then slice at frame-aligned sample boundaries into stems/<chapter>.music.f32.wav, each exactly its scene's length. Cache by hash of (identity, plan, timeline, narration WAV digests, crate version). Hard rules 4-8 of §7.3 enforced (attacks, cue density, no identical buffer within 10 s via round-robin + seeded micro-variation, pentagon-safe cue pitches, no melodic phrase starting under speech).

Tests: determinism (same inputs, same bytes on one platform); chapter independence (editing chapter k's plan leaves other chapters' stem fingerprints unchanged within +-0.5 dB per third-octave per second); slices concatenate to the act render exactly; stem length == scene samples.
Credit rules (AGENTS.md "Honest Credit"): real code and real tests in the same unit of work; no mocks or recorded fixtures presented as live proof; never weaken an assertion or regenerate a golden to get green; close only with evidence bound to a commit.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Candidate U-18 (evidence for the owner, not filed): fmn's 8-bit NV12 wire biases chroma. Repro at e2eec632: render a flat #0E1116 background with x264 CRF 0 (lossless), decode to yuv420p: Y 30, Cb 129, Cr 126; exact BT.709 limited codes are 30.37/130.50/126.48 (Cb 1.5 codes low: blue lost, background reads green-black). fmn's RGBA8 frames are exact (PNG 14,17,22), fmn-frame::rgba_to_nv12's quant8 rounds correctly (it would write 130), and the P010 path writes 121/522/507 (exact); so the bias is in the renderer's fused NV12 conversion. Also from S-5: U-16 (camera-route MP4 with audio untested) now has a passing render through the kit's wrapper (AAC muxed, durations equal).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Correction to candidate U-18 (3851db4): the cause is in fmn-output/src/negotiate.rs encode_argv, which tags the output (-colorspace bt709 -color_range tv) but not the rawvideo input, so ffmpeg converts from its default matrix. The NV12 conversion itself is exact: NV12 bytes 30/130/126 through that argv shape decode as Cb 129, and through it with '-colorspace bt709 -color_range tv' before '-i -' they decode exact. Impact at e2eec632, lossless: #0E1116 Cb 130.5 -> 129; #FFD866 Cr 149.7 -> 146, Y 201.6 -> 203. Suggested upstream fix: emit the input's colour description in encode_argv. The corpus works around it in its runner.

comments.author: EmeraldOwl
comments.text:
Landed 34bbcfa (pushed to origin/main): LineGaps::Thought in crates/explainer_kit/src/narration.rs, opt-in per video through the new Explainer.line_gaps field (every video, the kit tests and the example set Constant; Video F is NOT opted in until the owner's A/B; mental_math has a test that pins that and says to update it when he decides).
What it does: classify_gap(prev, next) from the two lines' text (Topic: next opens with Your turn / Take / Here's / Last one / One more / Most / The next, on a word boundary; Continuation: next opens with And/But/So/Then/Now/Because/Which/Plus/Or/That's, or the line before ends unfinished (a closing quote or bracket after the end mark does not hide the end); Beat: the rest); gap = audible silence 0.58 / 0.81 / 0.99 s (T-007 + P-4 human numbers) minus the two takes' own quiet edges (quiet_edges: T-007's detector, measured at load from the WAVs only under Thought), floor 0.10 s. A chapter's first line is placed by the class of the pair across the chapter join, from its lead only (Script::select keeps the full script, so a partial render opens where the whole render does). Authored windows (music_breath, listen, sonify) keep their length and their breath; hold never waits longer than BREATH, so whatever an author puts after a hold keeps its place (a continuation shortens it to 0.58 s). Cue waits keyed to a line's start or end (said_at, sentence_at, length) move with the lines by construction; the one BREATH constant outside the kit (mental_math bethe.rs, a wait up to a listen window) is keyed to the window, which keeps BREATH, so it stays right. check_gap_spread/gap_cv/MIN_GAP_CV=0.10 is the QA: Video F's plain gaps varied by about 0.04 under the constant rule, the classes on its real script by 0.16.
Tests (all new, real code): unit tests in narration.rs: classification table with planted negatives (a connective is the whole first word, an opener is a phrase not a prefix), quiet_edges on synthetic takes at 24 and 48 kHz with negatives (no silence, a 30 ms lead under the 40 ms run, silence only, shorter than a frame, a soft word 12 dB under the voice is not silence), line_gap/gap_before with real WAV takes (class minus tail minus lead, the floor, the constant rule ignoring text, window/first-line/video-first-line states), partial render equals whole render, constant gaps fail the spread check. Integration (tests/narrated_scene.rs): a frame-exact narrated scene under both rules (Constant reproduces the old placement 36/87/138/189/300, windows at 240; Thought 36/86/150/225/336, window 276, the line after it exactly 60 frames later in both), and a chapter rendered alone against the whole (60 vs 36 frames). mental_math: the ten plain pairs of ch 02 and 07 get the classes the P-4 pilot built (BEAT 02_1>2, 02_7>8, 07_1>2; CONT 02_2>3, 02_3>4, 02_5>6, 02_8>9; TOPIC 07_2>3, 07_4>5, 07_5>6), the 13 chapter joins open as all three classes, planned gaps of the whole script pass the spread check and constant BREATH fails it. Mutation check: removing the hold's min(BREATH) fails the integration test ([86,150] against [86,137]).
Gates, run on the build host in a private scratch tree (laptop tree rsynced, peers' dirty explainer_score/score files back at HEAD, own CARGO_TARGET_DIR): cargo fmt -p explainer_kit -p mental_math_explainer --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- D warnings Finished (kit, score and all 11 video crates); cargo test -p explainer_kit: lib 69 passed (55 before, 14 new) and every integration test ok, incl. narrated_scene 8/8; cargo test -p mental_math_explainer 36 passed; ubs on the 5 files I changed in substance: exit 0, 0 critical (warnings +85, almost all unwrap/assert in the new tests; two real ones fixed: direct indexing in opens_with and quiet_edges). cargo fmt --all --check shows one diff in crates/explainer_score/src/qa.rs, a peer's dirty file, not mine.
Not done / open: (1) the chapter tail is still the video's own constant (mental_math END_HOLD_S via music_breath), so only the lead of a chapter varies with the class (0.58 / 0.81 / 0.99 s less the lead, instead of the constant 0.6 s): joins that were ten copies of 3.52 s become 3.3-3.9 s; varying the tail is video code. (2) hold now stops short of a beat or a topic (it waits at most BREATH), so the picture's wipe can precede the next line's voice by up to 0.4 s of empty stage; if the owner dislikes that, hold can wait the full class gap at the cost of shifting an authored window that follows it. (3) in-line sentence gaps (the P-1 question) are narration assembly in tools/narration.py, not this bead. (4) no render or listening: the owner's A/B decides; to turn it on set Explainer.line_gaps to LineGaps::Thought in a video's main.rs and update the mental_math pin test.
